groups.instructions: Complete the notes below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage for each answer.
groups.strategy: Notes follow passage order. 'A NUMBER' means digits count separately from words: '15' is one number, so '15 degrees' = one number + one word = allowed.

questions.prompt: Latitude could be calculated from the sun at midday or the ________ at night.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1: 'the position of the Pole Star at night'.

questions.prompt: One hour of time difference = ________ of longitude.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1: 'each hour of difference … corresponds to 15 degrees of longitude'.

questions.prompt: On ships, temperature and ________ affected the accuracy of clocks.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1: 'changes in temperature and humidity caused metal parts to expand'.

questions.prompt: Many sailors on long voyages died of ________.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2: 'while their crews died of scurvy'.

questions.prompt: Longitude Act: prize of £20,000; method had to be accurate to within half a ________.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2: 'to within half a degree'. Notice the note already gives 'half a', so you only need one word — copying 'half a degree' into the gap would make the sentence wrong.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

questions.prompt: The disaster off the Scilly Isles was the only reason the Longitude Act was passed.
questions.explanation: The Act was passed 'partly in response to such disasters' — 'partly' contradicts 'the only reason'.
questions.trap: Watch absolute words in statements: only, always, never, all.

questions.prompt: The lunar distance method was based on incorrect scientific principles.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3: 'The method was sound in principle'. The difficulty was practical (tables, calculation time).

questions.prompt: Harrison's earliest clocks were made mainly of wood.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4: 'building his first clocks almost entirely from wood'.

questions.prompt: Harrison's fourth timekeeper was copied by watchmakers in France.
questions.explanation: France is never mentioned. The passage mentions later chronometers 'based on Harrison's principles' but nothing about French copies.

groups.instructions: Look at the following statements and the list of people/groups below. Match each statement with the correct person or group, A–D.
groups.strategy: Scan for each name and read the sentences around EVERY mention — the information about one person is often spread across paragraphs.

questions.prompt: produced a publication that reduced the time needed for a rival method
questions.explanation: Maskelyne 'published a nautical almanac that made lunar calculations considerably quicker'.

questions.prompt: checked the performance of a timekeeper himself
questions.explanation: 'King George III, who personally tested one of Harrison's watches'.

questions.prompt: questioned whether a success could be repeated
questions.explanation: The Board 'doubted whether a single successful watch proved that the method could be reproduced'.
questions.trap: Maskelyne was a member of the Board, but the passage attributes this doubt to the Board as a whole.

questions.prompt: developed a device to deal with the effects of heat and cold
questions.explanation: Harrison introduced 'a strip made from two different metals that compensated for changes in temperature'.
